participants: Chris Klevan (sales manager, ran the meeting)
Andrew Musial (closer, appears in diarization as 'Andrew Jin (Primal Instinct)'; released early at 00:13:51)
Adam A. (setter, new — introduced on this call)
Derek Harris (setter, starting on dials the following day)
summary: Fifty-eight-minute daily sales meeting: wins, projections for each rep, onboarding logistics for two new setters, then an extended role-play and coaching block with Richard Claessen on selling to high performers. A second new setter, Adam A., was introduced — 27, two years in sales, self-selected into setting over closing. Derek Harris was given his KPI of three sets per day and a projection built on a stated 20% set-to-close ratio. Andrew was carrying 20K cash and four units for the week against a target needing two more units; Richard was on one unit and $1,200 cash collected. The operational thread was that phone numbers captured at booking are not flowing through to the closers, which is blocking the pre-call confirmation the team believes drives show rate. In the coaching block Chris taught that the consequence frame does not work on prideful high performers and should be replaced with playing out the future at their peak, and that questions must be reframed so they do not read as challenges to a high performer's self-image. Two exchanges on this call are materially more important than the sales content: setters confirming they speak as Trevor in voice messages, and the manager declining to rule out stimulant use by closers.
notable: Setters send voice messages in the persona of Trevor, the coach and brand principal, and the manager confirmed it without objection. Richard: 'And you're Trevor, right? Like, you're Trevor. Just to check.' Adam: 'I'm Trevor?' Richard: 'Yeah, as in, like, you talk as Trevor in the VMs.' Adam: 'Oh, yeah. I talk as Trevor.' Chris: 'Sweet. Awesome. Good stuff.' This is the single most consequential item in this batch of internal calls and it directly answers the pilot's open question about how setters identify themselves.

The title suffixes in this corpus are explained here. Setters manually add their initials to the calendar event after booking: 'you edit it, you put your initials on there, you hit don't send... Just makes it so the closers know it's a set, and when there's double booking, it makes it very easy on a quick glance to just know which call they're going to try and prioritize.' KFS, KL and DH are setter initials on calendar events, not codes assigned centrally. Derek Harris starts dialling the day after this call, which bounds DH forward of 2026-07-09.

Stated KPIs and conversion benchmarks: 'the KPI is three sets per day'; 'three units, because that'll be about 20% set to close'; 'so 10 units for the month'. Use the 20% figure as the company's own set-to-close expectation when reconciling this corpus.

Cash per unit is running well below list. Andrew: '20K cash, four units so far this week' averages $5,000 a unit against a $6,000 price. Richard: 'We've got one unit, we've got 1,200 cash collected.' Any revenue rollup built on list price will overstate collections materially.

Payment plans are being extended ad hoc beyond anything documented. Richard on a deal he thought he had lost: 'There's a big chance I can still get him in on Friday, because he cannot pay in two times. It doesn't say he cannot pay in six times.'

The manager instructed a rep to omit the Consequence Frame for a whole prospect segment: 'I would play out the future of what it would like for them to be operating at their peak. I would not consequence them... consequence doesn't really work on people in Pride.' Phase 5 carries a weight of 20 in the scored playbook, so this is sanctioned deviation and should be read alongside every optimizer-type call in the corpus where P5 is missing.

Richard described a prospect's safety disclosure as a commercial advantage: 'I had this call yesterday with a firefighter. Like, he was like, yeah, I'm just, I'm really not showing up well. I'm not helping the people. Like, I'm putting other people at risk. It's so easy to then close them.'
Geographic financing disparity noted by a closer: 'maybe I get more Europeans, they're a little bit harder to close because they don't have financing.'

A booking exists in the calendar under the setter's own name and phone number. Adam: 'The first one that I did it, I put my name and my phone number, and then I just booked it myself.' Chris: 'No, yeah, you don't want to put your own stuff in there.' At least one calendar entry in this period is not a real prospect.

Show-rate mechanics: closers cannot pre-confirm DM-sourced sets because the phone number captured at booking is not reaching the system. Richard: 'I don't get a phone number... if I would want to confirm myself, just like, hey, just already introduced myself, as I also try to do with Kim's sets, sort of increasing the show rate even more, because then at least they know who I am.'

Coaching worth keeping: 'You're not here to create something that isn't there' recurs from the previous day, and Chris's reframe for high performers — 'what do you feel like is not quite at the level that you would like it to be?' rather than anything implying they are failing — is the most useful technique in either meeting.
